newsitem.title: UK: London Times readers rush for train ride offer. [CORRECTED 20:20 GMT]
newsitem.headline: London Times readers rush for train ride offer. [CORRECTED 20:20 GMT]

text.p: A promotion of a free ride on the Eurostar under-Channel rail express between London and Paris or Brussels has provoked a run on Britain's Times newspaper as readers scramble to accumulate tokens.
Newsagents said on Thursday that some people were bulk buying the paper, which is published by News International Plc, a subsidiary of Rupert Murdoch's News Corp.
"It's the train offer," said one newspaper vendor in south London. "Normally I have about 19 copies to sell a day, now I'm selling 50 with some people buying five copies at a time."

But Eurostar said it had no fear of repeating the now infamous mistake made three years ago by Hoover, the then British subsidiary of U.S. white goods group Maytag Corp, which encountered a costly stampede for free air tickets being offered to customers buying vacuum cleaners.
News International said it had increased its daily print run by between 150,000 and 180,000.
Figures of those proportions have raised the prospect of up to a million people lining up to claim free train tickets.
"We are now printing over a million copies a day and selling over 900,000 a day," circulation manager James Searby said.

Hoover's attempts to boost business ended in disaster as thousands of people rushed to buy vacuums to get a free pair of air tickets to the United States. Maytag eventually sold off Hoover's European operations to family-owned Candy SpA of Italy.

Eurostar spokesman Roger Harrison said: "We control the allocation, unlike Hoover. We say how many people we can take on what trains." He added: "We have a demand management system as airlines do with lots of cheap fares but only a certain number of seats are sold at the cheap fares."

Eurostar said it would be delighted if it had claims for a million free tickets, nearly a sixth (corrects from "nearly half") of its current annual traffic, but it expected a redemption rate far below that figure.

Eurostar's offer is for single tickets per household, not pairs, and booking times are subject to availability. Bookings must be made 10 days before travel and between December 6 and April 16, 1997. Travel must be completed by next April 30.
"There is plenty of room for lots of Times readers and they will bring a (paying) relative or friend with them because there is only one offer per household," Harrison said.
Newspaper readers must collect tokens published in 18 editions of daily The Times and three tokens from the weekly Sunday Times to qualify for the offer.
Eurostar has been trying to boost traffic since the British arm of the venture with the French and Belgian national railways was sold to the London and Continental Railways (L&CR) group.
L&CR includes Richard Branson's Virgin Group which took over in April with techniques employed by his airline to manage Eurostar's fare structures and marketing.
L&CR has said it needs to boost traffic to more than 10 million passengers a year if it is to fund the service's planned $5 billion fast rail link from London to the Channel Tunnel.
Eurostar said demand increased on an annualised basis from 3.9 million to 6.4 million passengers in the year to end-August.
